question: Why did the average cost of motor claims in New South Wales go up from June 2026?

grade.reason: Nothing to find: scored by the LLM grader.

report.interpretation: Average claim cost is incurred (paid plus open reserve) divided by claim count, by loss date. It covers NSW motor claims. I compared Jan–May 2026 with Jun–Aug 2026. September is left out because it is incomplete (about 79% reported). The monthly series is noisy, so I used these two multi-month blocks.
report.answer: The rise is real. NSW motor average cost was about $7,873 per claim for Jan–May 2026 and about $11,992 for Jun–Aug, up roughly 52%. The median rose too, from $5,525 to $9,051, so a few large claims don't explain it. The rise is mainly in collision claims, which averaged $8,663 before June and $13,027 from June. The share of collision claims above $15k went from 17.1% to 30.6%. The increase shows up across every repair shop, most adjusters, all channels and all metros, so no single shop, adjuster or location explains it. No NSW weather event is recorded for the period. Theft claims were also expensive in August (average about $36.6k), which pushed that month's average to $14.3k. I can't tell from the data why collision repairs got dearer. Plausible causes are higher repair costs or a change in the type of loss, and the data here can't separate them. September's average fell back to $6,978, but that month is incomplete.
report.answer_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT c.*, coalesce(pay.paid,0)+c.reserve_amount AS inc FROM claims c LEFT JOIN (SELECT claim_id,sum(amount) paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY 1) pay USING(claim_id) WHERE c.product='motor' AND c.state='NSW' AND loss_date>='2026-01-01' AND loss_date<'2026-09-01') SELECT loss_date>='2026-06-01' AS from_june, count(*) claims, round(avg(inc)) avg_cost, round(median(inc)) median_cost FROM s GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

Collision averages rose at all six shops (e.g. RS-001 $8.9k to $13.0k, RS-003 $7.0k to $11.9k). RS-006 is the highest at $22.3k but has only 8 claims.

hypotheses.evidence: Collision averages rose in 8 of 9 adjusters (ADJ-005 fell), in all three channels and in all three metros.
Collision is still the largest cause, and its own average rose. Theft was very high in August ($36.6k) but is a small group.
No duplicate claim rows. The 32 payments loaded outside nightly batches fall in May, which was a low month. September is incomplete and was excluded.

data_quality_issues.impact: May was a low-cost month, so this doesn't explain the June rise, but it is worth checking.

tool_calls.sql:
WITH source AS (
    SELECT c.*, p.channel, p.metro,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) AS paid_to_date,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) + c.reserve_amount AS incurred,
           c.close_date - c.report_date AS days_to_close
    FROM claims c
    JOIN policies p USING (policy_id)
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) AS paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY claim_id
    ) pay USING (claim_id)
)
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', loss_date) AS DATE) AS period, sum(incurred) / count(*) AS value
FROM source
WHERE loss_date >= DATE '2025-10-01'
  AND loss_date <= DATE '2026-09-30'
  AND product IN ('motor')
  AND state IN ('NSW')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL

SELECT loss_date>='2026-06-01' AS from_june, count(*) claims, round(avg(inc)) avg_cost, round(avg(inc) FILTER (WHERE cause='collision')) collision_avg, round(median(inc)) median_cost FROM s GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
